title: Why banjo players switched to guitar in the early thirties
summary: Goodwin says the resonator guitar was mellow, better for singers and combos, and banjos were hard to record.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: Oh, here's a question for you, Crook. They're asking about switching of instruments; clarinets, switching from an Albert to a Boehm [system], cornet to trumpet. Here's one. When did most banjo players switch to
What was the reason for that?
Well, the guitar began to be amplified -- well, not at the start, see, but they had -- they had a guitar with a steel back on it and it had a resonator on it and it could be heard in small combos.
Surely a banjo could be heard in small combos.

The banjo could be heard in the small or any kind of combo. I remember at times you would go to record and they had no way of muffling the banjo. Most guys didn't know about the -- they had a mute for a banjo that I had learned about almost the time when I was ready to stop playing banjo; but it didn't work out so good and this -- you'd go to record and they would make you turn your back and play into the drapes so that you wouldn't cut through because that A string on a banjo, you could hear it miles, it seemed like. The guitar was a soft and mellow thing.
You could play more melody with it?
You could play more melody and --
You're talking about how many strings now?
Six, six-string guitar, Spanish guitar, and you could -- most singers liked the mellow tone

of the guitar. If you'll notice now, some singers just have a guitar accompaniment and it is a beautiful thing. I think it just began in the early '30s to realize what potential a guitar had as to be in a band because some bands had two guitars and this is the first starting of the guitar coming into prominence with a jazz band.
Because it was more melodic, it was not so harsh, not so penetrating?
For a while I doubled on guitar and banjo but that's pretty rough doubling going.
